title: Dão
description: A granite plateau ringed by mountains: elegant reds and Portugal's finest white grape, Encruzado.
L: Explain how mountains shape its climate

The Dão lies in central-northern Portugal, south of the Douro, on a granite plateau at 200 to 900 m. It's surrounded by mountains: Caramulo to the west, Buçaco, and the Serra da Estrela, Portugal's highest mainland range, to the south-east. Vineyards are scattered among pine forests, about 15,000 hectares.

The mountains block Atlantic rain from the west and continental heat from the east. Summers are warm and dry, winters cold and wet, with large day and night swings. Granite soils, sandy and poor, drain well. The result is wines with freshness, elegance and moderate alcohol, often compared with Burgundy in style.
What shapes the Dão's protected climate?
Mountains on all sides moderate rain and heat.

The Dão was demarcated in 1908, one of Portugal's oldest regions. For decades, co-operatives dominated, and quality declined. After Portugal joined the EU in 1986, private estates could make and sell their own wine again, and quality rose sharply. Today the Dão is known for elegance and age-worthy wines.
After 1986, private estates helped lift the Dão's quality.
Yes, after co-operatives had dominated for decades.
The Dão is a granite plateau ringed by mountains
Mountains give a fresh, balanced climate

Touriga Nacional probably originated in the Dão and must be at least 20% of the region's red blends. Jaen, the same as Spain's Mencía, gives soft, fruity, floral wines. Alfrocheiro gives colour and red fruit. Tinta Roriz, Tempranillo, adds structure. Dão reds are fresh, floral and structured, with red fruit, pine and spice.

Traditionally, Dão wines are blends, often from old field blend vineyards. Touriga Nacional gives aroma and structure; Jaen softness; Alfrocheiro colour; Tinta Roriz body. Single-varietal Touriga Nacional and Jaen are also common now.
Match each grape to its role.
Jaen is the same grape as Mencía, grown across the border in Spain's Bierzo and Ribeira Sacra.
Which grape is Jaen the same as?
Jaen and Mencía are the same grape.
Touriga Nacional probably originated in the Dão
Jaen, Alfrocheiro and Tinta Roriz complete the reds
Dão reds are fresh, floral and structured

Encruzado is a white grape native to the Dão, and grown almost nowhere else. It gives medium to full-bodied whites with citrus, white peach, pear, flowers and a mineral, sometimes smoky edge, with fresh acidity. It's often compared with white Burgundy for its texture and complexity.

Encruzado takes well to barrel fermentation and lees ageing, which add creaminess and nutty notes without masking its fruit. It resists oxidation well. Good Encruzado ages 10 years or more, developing honey, nuts and toast. It's also blended with Malvasia Fina, Bical and Cerceal-Branco in Dão whites.
Which white wine style is Encruzado often compared with?
For its texture, complexity and response to oak.

Encruzado shows that Portugal, known for reds and Port, can make world-class whites. It needs careful handling in the vineyard, as it's prone to some diseases, and yields must be controlled. Producers like Quinta dos Roques and Quinta da Pellada helped establish its reputation.
Encruzado is the Dão's native white
Barrel fermentation and lees add texture
It can age 10 years or more
Reading the Dão and eating with it

Labels show Dão DOC, sometimes Dão Nobre, a top category requiring higher quality and ageing, the producer, often a quinta, the grapes and Reserva or Garrafeira. Red Dão must include at least 20% Touriga Nacional. Many wines are blends with grapes listed on the back.

Dão reds suit roast kid, lamb, game, Portuguese rice dishes like arroz de pato, duck rice, and Serra da Estrela cheese, a creamy sheep's cheese from the nearby mountains. Encruzado suits bacalhau, grilled fish, roast chicken and creamy dishes. Serve reds at 16 to 17, whites at 10 to 12.
Which cheese, from nearby mountains, suits Dão wines?
A creamy sheep's cheese from Portugal's highest mountains.
Dão reds age gracefully. A 10-year-old Dão Reserva often shows red fruit, pine and leather in perfect balance.
Dão reds must include at least 20% Touriga Nacional.
Labels show DOC, Dão Nobre and Reserva
